lessons.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
lessons.summary: Audio adaptation of Anthropic’s Scion post: why git broke at 30k merges/day, how a changeset-based VCS and three-tier cache replaced mirrors, and why they still don’t want you to fork git.

quiz.q: Why did git’s design become the bottleneck rather than a feature?
quiz.a: Git assumes complete offline clones; Anthropic’s always-online agents and CI hit ~100 GB history tens of millions of times a day, which mirrors could not absorb.

quiz.q: What is a Scion changeset compared with a git commit?
quiz.a: A write-ahead-log entry of files changed vs the first parent plus content-addressed blobs, not a full tree; blame and history are derived data.

quiz.q: What do they want other companies to copy?
quiz.a: Not Scion itself—server-side source-control APIs, cacheable immutable fetches, and sparse checkouts that compose inside git forges.
